examples.raw:
SELECT S.semester_id, T.semester_name 
FROM Semesters T 
JOIN Student_Enrolment S ON T.semester_id = S.semester_id 
GROUP BY S.semester_id, T.semester_name 
ORDER BY COUNT(S.student_id) DESC 
LIMIT 1;
examples.pred: SELECT S.semester_id, T.semester_name FROM Semesters T JOIN Student_Enrolment S ON T.semester_id = S.semester_id GROUP BY S.semester_id, T.semester_name ORDER BY COUNT(S.student_id) DESC LIMIT 1

examples.question: For each semester, what is the name and id of the one with the most students registered?
examples.gold: SELECT T1.semester_name ,  T1.semester_id FROM Semesters AS T1 JOIN Student_Enrolment AS T2 ON T1.semester_id  =  T2.semester_id GROUP BY T1.semester_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1
examples.raw:
SELECT S.semester_id, D.semester_name
FROM Semesters S
JOIN (
    SELECT semester_id, COUNT(*) as student_count
    FROM Student_Enrolment
    GROUP BY semester_id
) E ON S.semester_id = E.semester_id
WHERE E.student_count = (
    SELECT MAX(student_count)
    FROM (
        SELECT COUNT(*) as student_count
        FROM Student_Enrolment
        GROUP BY semester_id
    ) E2
)
GROUP BY S.semester_id, D.semester_name;
examples.pred: SELECT S.semester_id, D.semester_name FROM Semesters S JOIN ( SELECT semester_id, COUNT(*) as student_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY semester_id ) E ON S.semester_id = E.semester_id WHERE E.student_count = ( SELECT MAX(student_count) FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) as student_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY semester_id ) E2 ) GROUP BY S.semester_id, D.semester_name
